assignments.text:
The sea has no appreciation of great men, but knocks them about like
the small fry. It is habitually hard upon Sir Leicester, whose
countenance it greenly mottles in the manner of sage-cheese and in
whose aristocratic system it effects a dismal revolution. It is the
Radical of Nature to him. Nevertheless, his dignity gets over it
after stopping to refit, and he goes on with my Lady for Chesney
Wold, lying only one night in London on the way to Lincolnshire.
assignments.summary: Sir Leicester becomes ill at sea, which temporarily diminishes his dignity, though it recovers before they reach Chesney Wold.
assignments.best_quote: The sea has no appreciation of great men, but knocks them about like the small fry. It is habitually hard upon Sir Leicester, whose countenance it greenly mottles in the manner of sage-cheese.

assignments.text:
His passion was fearful. I could not have believed in such rage
without seeing it.
assignments.summary: Esther notes that Gridley's passion is fearful and seemingly unbelievable without witnessing it directly.
assignments.best_quote: His passion was fearful. I could not have believed in such rage without seeing it.

assignments.text:
So Guster, much impressed by regarding herself for the time as the
handmaid of Chadband, whom she knows to be endowed with the gift of
holding forth for four hours at a stretch, prepares the little
drawing-room for tea. All the furniture is shaken and dusted, the
portraits of Mr. and Mrs. Snagsby are touched up with a wet cloth,
the best tea-service is set forth, and there is excellent provision
made of dainty new bread, crusty twists, cool fresh butter, thin
slices of ham, tongue, and German sausage, and delicate little rows
of anchovies nestling in parsley, not to mention new-laid eggs, to be
brought up warm in a napkin, and hot buttered toast. For Chadband is
rather a consuming vessel—the persecutors say a gorging vessel—and
can wield such weapons of the flesh as a knife and fork remarkably
well.
assignments.summary: Guster carefully prepares an elaborate tea with rich foods, anticipating that Chadband is a voracious eater despite his spiritual calling.

assignments.text:
“What do you think, now,” says Mr. Guppy, “about—you don’t mind
Smallweed?”
assignments.summary: Guppy begins offering Jobling advice and opportunities, checking if Smallweed's presence is acceptable.

assignments.text:
“I mean,” returns Mr. Guppy, shrugging his shoulders with becoming
modesty, “that I can’t make him out. I appeal to our mutual friend
Smallweed whether he has or has not heard me remark that I can’t make
him out.”
assignments.summary: Guppy admits he cannot fathom Krook's nature and appeals to Smallweed to confirm his mystification.

assignments.text: “Dining at his expense, Bart?”
assignments.summary: Bart nods again.

assignments.text:
Mademoiselle goes out with an air of native gentility; and Mr.
Bucket, to whom it is, on an emergency, as natural to be groom of the
ceremonies as it is to be anything else, shows her downstairs, not
without gallantry.
assignments.summary: Mademoiselle Hortense exits with air and grace; Bucket escorts her downstairs with gallantry.
assignments.best_quote: Mademoiselle goes out with an air of native gentility

assignments.text:
“No, miss, nor I can’t help it,” says Charley. “And if you please,
miss, Mr. Jarndyce’s love, and he thinks you’ll like to teach me now
and then. And if you please, Tom and Emma and me is to see each other
once a month. And I’m so happy and so thankful, miss,” cried Charley
with a heaving heart, “and I’ll try to be such a good maid!”
assignments.summary: Charley continues to explain Jarndyce's kindness and his hope that Esther will teach her, and reports their plan for monthly reunions.
assignments.best_quote: And Mr. Jarndyce's love, and he thinks you'll like to teach me now and then.

assignments.text:
“Now, I may say to your ladyship at once,” says Mr. Guppy, a little
emboldened, “it is no matter arising out of Jarndyce and Jarndyce
that made me so desirous to speak to your ladyship, which conduct I
have no doubt did appear, and does appear, obtrusive—in fact, almost
blackguardly.”
assignments.summary: Guppy insists his purpose is unrelated to Jarndyce and Jarndyce.

assignments.text:
Mr. Jellyby could not hear what she said, but he seemed very low
indeed and shed tears, I thought.
assignments.summary: Esther notes that Mr. Jellyby seems very low and appears to shed tears.

assignments.text:
Then I made one, and Charley made one, and the pen wouldn’t join
Charley’s neatly, but twisted it up into a knot.
assignments.summary: Both Esther and Charley practice making the letter O, with the pen creating a knot.

assignments.text: “No,” says Mrs. Snagsby.
assignments.summary: Mrs. Snagsby refuses the drink.

assignments.text: “Are the pictures all as they used to be?” I asked her.
assignments.summary: Esther asks if the pictures remain unchanged.

assignments.text: “But not a dreary place at present, my lord,” said Mr. Kenge.
assignments.summary: Kenge politely contradicts the Chancellor, noting the house is not currently dreary.

assignments.text:
But I knew it, I knew it well now. It came upon me as the close of
the benignant history I had been pursuing, and I felt that I had but
one thing to do. To devote my life to his happiness was to thank him
poorly, and what had I wished for the other night but some new means
of thanking him?
assignments.summary: Esther understands that accepting Jarndyce's proposal is the culmination of her transformation and the best way to thank him for his love.
assignments.best_quote: To devote my life to his happiness was to thank him poorly, and what had I wished for the other night but some new means of thanking him?

assignments.text:
“No, sir, no. Robbed me? He did nothing but what was kind-hearted by
me, and that’s the wonder of it.”
assignments.summary: The woman insists Jo did nothing but act kindly to her.

assignments.text:
“Why, she is not well-bred, you see,” returns Mr. Rouncewell with
some quickness in his manner, as if he were glad to have the lawyer
to retort upon, “and she is an inexperienced little thing and knows
no better. If she had remained here, sir, she would have improved, no
doubt.”
assignments.summary: Rouncewell attributes Rosa's distress to her being ill-bred and inexperienced, suggesting she would have improved had she remained.

assignments.text: “I do not quite understand you.”
assignments.summary: Lady Dedlock claims not to understand him fully.

assignments.text:
The purblind day was feebly struggling with the fog when I opened my
eyes to encounter those of a dirty-faced little spectre fixed upon
me. Peepy had scaled his crib, and crept down in his bed-gown and
cap, and was so cold that his teeth were chattering as if he had cut
them all.
assignments.summary: In the early morning, Peepy climbs out of his crib and approaches Esther shivering with cold.

assignments.text:
“Your cousin, Mr. Jarndyce. I owe so much to him. Would you mind
describing him to me?”
assignments.summary: Esther thanks Ada for welcoming her and asks her to describe their cousin Mr. Jarndyce, to whom Esther feels greatly indebted.

assignments.text: “Not at all,” I would assure him.
assignments.summary: Esther denies being fatigued.

assignments.text:
“Why, my love!” I remonstrated. “Ada, why should you not speak to
us!”
assignments.summary: Esther asks Ada why she should hesitate to speak freely.

assignments.text: “’Tis curious,” said he. “And yet I thought so at the time!”
assignments.summary: George says he found something curious and that he suspected it at the time.

assignments.text:
Volumnia wishes of all things to know what is doing? Whether they are
going to convict, or whatever it is, that dreadful soldier? Whether
he had any accomplices, or whatever the thing is called in the law?
And a great deal more to the like artless purpose.
assignments.summary: Volumnia eagerly asks Bucket whether they will convict the soldier and if he had accomplices.

assignments.text:
“Aye, and even in gen-teel families, in high families, in great
families,” says Mr. Bucket, again gravely eyeing Sir Leicester aside.
“I have had the honour of being employed in high families before, and
you have no idea—come, I’ll go so far as to say not even YOU have
any idea, sir,” this to the debilitated cousin, “what games goes on!”
assignments.summary: Bucket alludes darkly to the scandalous secrets he has uncovered in aristocratic households.
assignments.best_quote: Aye, and even in gen-teel families, in high families, in great families, I have had the honour of being employed in high families before, and you have no idea what games goes on!

assignments.text:
“I don’t care for that. I want to know who’s got ’em. And I tell you
what we want—what we all here want, Mr. Bucket. We want more
painstaking and search-making into this murder. We know where the
interest and the motive was, and you have not done enough. If George
the vagabond dragoon had any hand in it, he was only an accomplice,
and was set on. You know what I mean as well as any man.”
assignments.summary: Smallweed demands more thorough investigation and suggests George was merely an accomplice used by someone else.
assignments.best_quote: If George the vagabond dragoon had any hand in it, he was only an accomplice, and was set on.

assignments.text:
“She had better go. Her hands should be the first to touch her. They
have a higher right than ours.”
assignments.summary: Woodcourt affirms that Esther has a higher right than anyone else to be the first to touch her mother.
assignments.best_quote: Her hands should be the first to touch her. They have a higher right than ours.

assignments.text:
“Yes,” said my guardian, nodding his head. He had put his arm about
me as if there were something to protect me from and looked in my
face, smiling.
assignments.summary: John Jarndyce affirms her answer while embracing her protectively and looking at her with a smile.

assignments.text:
“Brother, I thank you a million times for your more than brotherly
welcome, and a million times more to that for your more than
brotherly intentions. But my plans are made. Before I say a word as
to them, I wish to consult you upon one family point. How,” says the
trooper, folding his arms and looking with indomitable firmness at
his brother, “how is my mother to be got to scratch me?”
assignments.summary: George insists his mother must remove him from her will before he will agree to any arrangements.
assignments.best_quote: how is my mother to be got to scratch me?

assignments.text:
Richard smiled and lifted up his arm to touch him as he stood behind
the head of the couch.
assignments.summary: Richard attempts to touch John Jarndyce in gratitude.

assignments.text:
My husband drew a little nearer towards Ada, and I saw him solemnly
lift up his hand to warn my guardian.
assignments.summary: Allan discretely signals to John Jarndyce that Richard is approaching death.

assignments.text:
“Most assuredly not!” said Mr. Boythorn, clapping him on the shoulder
with an air of protection that had something serious in it, though he
laughed. “He will stand by the low boy, always. Jarndyce, you may
rely upon him! But speaking of this trespass—with apologies to Miss
Clare and Miss Summerson for the length at which I have pursued so
dry a subject—is there nothing for me from your men Kenge and
Carboy?”
assignments.summary: Boythorn passionately assures Mr. Jarndyce that he will always support Richard, calling back to their school friendship, then apologizes for discussing trespass at length and asks about legal correspondence.
assignments.best_quote: He will stand by the low boy, always. Jarndyce, you may rely upon him!
